newsitem.title: LITHUANIA: ERICSSON TO STEP UP LITHUANIA OPERATIONS.
newsitem.headline: ERICSSON TO STEP UP LITHUANIA OPERATIONS.

text.p: Swedish telecoms group AB LM Ericsson said on Wednesday sales in Lithuania would increase 60 percent this year from 1996 levels of $12 million and that it would spend $5 million on its Lithuania operations in 1997.

"In Lithuania in 1996 activities corresponded to sales of around $12 million. You could say it's not very much...but we see the growth. For 1997 this will grow by at least 60 percent," Ericsson Denmark president Bjorn Olsson told a news conference.
Ericsson said that its activities in Lithuania were the most successful in the Baltic states and Poland.
"Another measure of our activity is what is the expenditure of what Ericsson is putting into our operations in Lithuania," Olsson said.
Expenses from 1992 to 1996 totalled around $3 million, Olsson said.
"We decided for another $5 million in 1997," he said.
He said the rise was because of increasing levels of activity in Lithuania as well as for employee training and a new Ericsson office.
"We are here to stay and plan to expand with the expansion of the telecommunications sector in Lithuania," Olsson said.
The number of Ericsson employees in Lithuania would increase to between 45 and 50 in 1997 from around 35, Ericsson said in a statement. Most of these would be technicians and engineers.
Asked if Ericsson would participate in the privatisation of Lithuania's telecoms sector, the company said no because it was interested in the supply side instead of operations.

Ericsson's major customers in Lithuania include Lithuanian Telecom, to which it supplies its AXE switching equipment. Ericsson said in a statement that it would begin implementing 13 new exchanges on April 1.
Another customer is mobile telephone operator Bite GSM, Lithuanian Energy, Lithuanian Railways and Mazeikiu Nafta.
